book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Likely Outcomes & Our Action Plan
question: Weighing the Bull and Bear steelmen against our Pass 1 forensic audit and Stage 4 tape, why is new capital REJECTED (TIER_0), why do we immediately trim 9 of our 18 Zerodha shares under EXIT_ON_BOUNCE, and where does capital redeploy?

epigraph.quote: Good investing is not about defending yesterday's verdict; it is about aligning business quality, normalized valuation, and price trend before committing—or retaining—every rupee.
epigraph.author: Institutional Portfolio Committee Charter

web_blocks.html: An honest refresh strips away status-quo bias and follows the updated evidence. Apar Industries retained its price-blind COMPOUNDER_PASS (kpi_health: PASS_WITH_WATCH) on its ₹15,025+ Cr order book, 11.0% Q2 cable EBITDA margin, and post-QIP CARE AA balance sheet [21, 22, 24]. Yet two new realities—Pass 1's discovery that 67% of Q2 EBITDA growth came from a non-normal Specialty Oils windfall alongside -9.2% conductor volume, -29.7% U.S. revenue, and -₹862.63 Cr H1 CFO [21, 23], combined with a deepening Stage 4 breakdown (CAP_REJECTED, -34.99% 28-day RS, 7 distribution days) [26, 28]—compel a stricter stance.

67% (+₹194 Cr) of Q2 EBITDA growth was a non-normal TSO windfall (₹23,262/KL on -20% volume); conductor volume fell -9.2% YoY and premium mix slipped to 39.4% [21, 23].
Headline TTM EPS overstates repeatable profit; strip out TSO windfalls and model ₹36,500–₹37,000/MT conductor spreads.
Aug 2026 ₹2,500 Cr QIP lifted equity to ₹8,520 Cr, cut formal D/E to 0.12x, and earned CARE AA; Stable [22, 26].
H1 FY27 CFO was -₹862.63 Cr; FY26 working capital hit ₹8,520 Cr (~37% TOI) with ~88% NFB limit utilization, forcing ₹1,875 Cr (75% of QIP) to fund working capital [22].
QIP prevented a liquidity crunch, but high working-capital intensity caps near-term free cash flow conversion.
US DOE $1.9B reconductoring program and India's 135 GW renewable grid approval create decade-long demand [21].

Q2 U.S. sales fell -29.7% YoY (total reported cable exports fell 45.2% YoY and U.S. cable sales fell 50% YoY) with >₹440 Cr cables in DDP transit and 54% vs ~10% non-metal tariff gap; DICABS grew Q2 sales +135% YoY [21, 23, 25].
Tariff asymmetry and resurgent domestic rivalry (DICABS) plus CTC Global / Hindalco input dependencies compress pricing power.
Pullback of -26.03% off peak brings price within +2.43% of rising 200-DMA (₹13,912.61) [26].
At 41.83x TTM P/E (19%–26% above Polycab 35.3x and KEI 33.1x), stock is in Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED, -12.21% below 50D SMA, -34.99% 28d RS) across a Stage 4 sector [26, 28].
Do not fight Stage 4 or pay 42x on windfall earnings: REJECT new capital, trim 9 held shares now, and exit the rest on bounce or stop.
web_blocks.takeaway: Great industrial franchise, but non-normal Q2 TSO windfall, negative H1 CFO (-₹862.63 Cr), U.S. tariff drag, and Stage 4 CAP_REJECTED breakdown eliminate any near-term risk-reward edge.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of truth, and an honest refresh must be willing to change its mind when the evidence changes. Over nine chapters, we confirmed that Apar Industries remains a high-quality industrial franchise—a global conductor leader with a ₹15,025+ Cr backlog, 11% cable margins, and a newly fortified CARE AA balance sheet. Yet Pass 1 and the late-November tape delivered two sobering blows that we cannot rationalize away.

First, on fundamentals: two-thirds of Q2 FY27's headline EBITDA growth came from an abnormal Specialty Oils windfall (₹23,262/KL on 20% lower volume) that management warned will not repeat, while conductor volumes fell 9.2%, U.S. sales dropped 29.7% (total reported cable exports fell 45.2% YoY and U.S. cable sales fell 50% YoY), H1 operating cash flow fell to -₹862.63 Cr, and 75% of the ₹2,500 Cr QIP had to be earmarked for working capital. Second, on the tape: APARINDS has sunk deeper into Stage 4 (-12.21% below its 50-DMA, -7.50% below its 30-week SMA, -34.99% 28-day RS, 7 distribution days) right alongside every major Indian electrical peer.

When we reconcile our scenarios directly to our Reverse DCF and Stage 4 peer multiples—20% Bull (₹17,500), 50% Base (₹13,800 at 33.25x normalized FY28E EPS ₹415, in line with KEI's 33.1x), and 30% Bear (₹9,600)—probability-weighted fair value is ₹13,280, or -6.81% below the live November 25 TradingView close of ₹14,250 (November 23 NSE ledger ₹14,184). Our new-capital verdict therefore downgrades cleanly to REJECTED (TIER_0; reasons: TREND, CASH_FLOW, VALUATION).

For our 18 existing Zerodha shares (₹15,259.13 average cost, ₹2,55,312 ledger value, -7.05% unrealized loss, 5.99% portfolio weight), we also confront a harsh arithmetic truth: waiting to sell all 18 shares on a bounce (+5.6% midpoint vs -7.52% stop) creates an unfavorable 0.75:1 asymmetry. We solve this cleanly under EXIT_ON_BOUNCE by trimming 9 shares immediately at market (₹14,184–₹14,250)—cutting Stage 4 portfolio weight in half to ~3.0% and slashing stop-gap dollar risk from -₹19,293 to -₹9,647 (0.23% of IN net worth)—and exiting the remaining 9 shares into any relief rally toward ₹14,805–₹15,302 or immediately below our upward-ratcheted ₹13,178.14 stop.

Let us walk through why this two-tranche exit is vastly superior to either passive holding or emotional all-at-once capitulation. If you hold all 18 shares passively hoping the 200-day SMA at ₹13,912.61 holds, a sudden gap below our ₹13,178.14 stop locks in a -₹19,293 additional drop from ₹14,250—on top of the -₹19,352 unrealized loss already sitting on the Zerodha ledger. By selling 9 shares immediately at market (~₹1,27,656–₹1,28,250), you immediately cut your Stage 4 exposure from 5.99% down to roughly 3.00% of our ₹42.60 lakh India portfolio and slice maximum remaining stop-loss risk in half to just 0.23% of net worth.

At the same time, keeping the remaining 9 shares behind a strict ₹13,178.14 daily-close stop lets us harvest any oversold reflex rally off the rising 40-week EMA (₹14,235) and 200-day SMA (₹13,913) back into the ₹14,805–₹15,302 resistance band. That captures roughly ₹5,000 to ₹9,466 of additional recovery on the second tranche without leaving full portfolio weight exposed to a Stage 4 waterfall toward our ₹9,600 Bear Case.

Finally, remember what opportunity cost actually means in a live portfolio. Our India book holds ₹15.39 lakh in cash alongside 17 active positions, and right now confirmed Stage 2 leaders are sitting inside actionable buy zones. Rotating freed Apar proceeds into 50% liquid INR cash, 30% COFORGE (Stage 2 VCP squeeze at ₹2,060 inside its ₹1,952–₹2,067 buy zone, +47.4% TTM EPS growth, 1.50:1 R:R toward ₹2,620), and 20% ZYDUSLIFE (Stage 2 at ₹1,236, 29.69x P/E, 1.51:1 R:R toward ₹1,420) systematically upgrades portfolio momentum, earnings quality, and risk-reward in a single disciplined sequence.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When waiting for a bounce risks -7.5% to capture +5.6% (0.75:1), holding full size is hope, not strategy. Trimming half immediately at market cuts portfolio risk in half today while letting the remaining 9 shares capture any 200-DMA reflex bounce.

book_subsections.title: Where Freed Capital Goes Next
paragraphs: Every rupee tied up in a Stage 4 laggard (-34.99% 28-day RS) is a rupee unavailable for confirmed Stage 2 leaders. As we trim 9 APARINDS shares immediately and exit the remaining 9 on a bounce or stop breach, our 100%-reconciled redeployment plan keeps 50% in liquid INR cash—respecting the contraction in Nifty 500 breadth to 55.2% above the 50-DMA—while rotating 30% into COFORGE (2026-11-25 TV close ₹2,060 / 2026-11-23 NSE close ₹2,142.30 inside its ₹1,952–₹2,067 Stage 2 VCP buy zone, 1.50:1 asymmetry toward ₹2,620) and 20% into ZYDUSLIFE (2026-11-25 TV ₹1,236 / 2026-11-23 NSE ₹1,199.50, Stage 2 CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION, 1.51:1 asymmetry toward ₹1,420). Electrical peer Polycab receives 0% because it is also trapped in Stage 4.

To remove emotion from execution, our 18-share Zerodha exit runs in two mechanical tranches: trim 9 shares immediately at market (₹14,184–₹14,250) to immediately capture ~₹1.28 lakh and cut Stage 4 exposure to ~3.0%, then sell the remaining 9 shares into the 20-day SMA / 10-week EMA supply band (₹14,805.30–₹15,301.76). If no relief bounce arrives and price closes below ₹13,178.14 on a daily or weekly basis, exit all remaining 9 shares immediately at market.

book_subsections.title: What Would Change Our Mind?
paragraphs: We remain open-minded if the facts improve. To cancel our remaining 9-share bounce exit or re-admit APARINDS for fresh capital, we require two simultaneous proofs: (1) a high-volume weekly reclaim above the 30-week SMA (₹15,405.10) that ends Stage 4 distribution, and (2) Q3 FY27 results demonstrating positive operating cash flow, liquidation of the ₹800 Cr U.S. DDP transit inventory, and conductor/cable EBITDA growth without a one-off Specialty Oils windfall.
